summary: Linear system with forcing that depends on t. There is no fixed direction field; the graph shows the solution curve when initial values are given.

methods.name: Shift the equilibrium
methods.reason: The forcing depends on \(t\), so there is no constant equilibrium to shift to.

methods.name: Variation of parameters (systems)
methods.reason: It works for any forcing once the homogeneous system is solved.

steps.title: Find a fundamental matrix
steps.text: The matrix exponential solves the homogeneous system and equals the identity at \(t = 0\).

steps.title: Set up the formula
steps.text: Looking for \(\mathbf{X} = \Phi(t)\,\mathbf{u}(t)\) gives \(\mathbf{u}' = \Phi^{-1}\mathbf{g}\). For the exponential, \(\Phi^{-1}(t) = e^{-At}\).

steps.title: Write the general solution
latex: x(t) = C_{1} \cos{\left(t \right)} + C_{2} \sin{\left(t \right)} + 1,\qquad y(t) = - C_{1} \sin{\left(t \right)} + C_{2} \cos{\left(t \right)} - t

steps.title: Apply the initial conditions
steps.text: Set \(t = 0\) and solve the equations for the constants.

steps.title: Check
steps.text: Checked by substituting back into every equation, and it meets the initial conditions.

methods.name: Eigenvalue method
methods.reason: This solves homogeneous systems \(\mathbf{X}' = A\mathbf{X}\); here there is a forcing term.

methods.name: Matrix exponential
methods.reason: This solves homogeneous systems \(\mathbf{X}' = A\mathbf{X}\); here there is a forcing term.
